pr.body: Interpolating queries as the initial step. Fixes #107530
pr.title: Query splitting: Interpolate queries at the start of the process

raw_findings.body: addAdHocFilters is executed twice on the same expression, so the query sent to Loki contains every ad-hoc label matcher/label filter duplicated (e.g. {a="b", x="y", x="y"}). It also re-runs templateSrv.replace on already-interpolated text, so variable values that themselves contain '$name' tokens get recursively re-interpolated.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Double application of a non-idempotent transformation (addAdHocFilters) produces duplicated filters in the executed query.
raw_findings.impact: addAdHocFilters is executed twice on the same expression, so the query sent to Loki contains every ad-hoc label matcher/label filter duplicated (e.g. {a="b", x="y", x="y"}). It also re-runs templateSrv.replace on already-interpolated text, so variable values that themselves contain '$name' tokens get recursively re-interpolated.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch moves interpolation to the start of runSplitQuery without removing or bypassing the existing applyTemplateVariables call performed later by DataSourceWithBackend.query for the same request.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Apply interpolation in only one layer: either strip request.filters/scopedVars from the sub-requests passed to runQuery so DataSourceWithBackend does not re-apply them, or mark targets as already interpolated (e.g. keep interpolation only in DataSourceWithBackend and interpolate only step/expr needed for calculateStep locally without adding ad-hoc filters).
raw_findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice: runSplitQuery and DataSourceWithBackend.query both apply applyTemplateVariables, duplicating ad-hoc filters
raw_findings.trigger: A user runs a Loki query with the lokiQuerySplitting feature toggle enabled while ad-hoc filters are active on the dashboard/Explore. runSplitQuery interpolates the targets here, then each sub-request flows through datasource.runQuery -> super.query() (DataSourceWithBackend.query, line 185), which calls applyTemplateVariables again with the same request.filters.

raw_findings.body: Ad-hoc filters are appended to the expression up to three times (previously the old interpolateVariablesInQueries call passed no adhocFilters, so filters were added only once by the backend layer), producing queries with duplicated label matchers sent to Loki on every shard sub-request.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The same query text is transformed repeatedly by a non-idempotent ad-hoc filter step across three nested layers.
raw_findings.impact: Ad-hoc filters are appended to the expression up to three times (previously the old interpolateVariablesInQueries call passed no adhocFilters, so filters were added only once by the backend layer), producing queries with duplicated label matchers sent to Loki on every shard sub-request.
raw_findings.root_cause: Replacing interpolateVariablesInQueries (called without ad-hoc filters) with applyTemplateVariables(query, scopedVars, request.filters) stacked on top of the identical new interpolation inside runSplitQuery and the existing backend-layer interpolation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Interpolate at exactly one layer: since runSplitQuery now interpolates, remove the map here (or pass a flag/pre-interpolated targets so downstream layers skip applyTemplateVariables), and prevent the DataSourceWithBackend re-application for sub-requests.
raw_findings.title: Shard-split path now applies applyTemplateVariables (including ad-hoc filters) three times per target
raw_findings.trigger: A sharded Loki query (lokiShardSplitting enabled) runs with ad-hoc filters set: runShardSplitQuery interpolates here with request.filters, then every sub-request is delegated to runSplitQuery which interpolates again (the updated test itself asserts applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times for one target), and DataSourceWithBackend.query applies it a third time.

raw_findings.body: The test certifies behavior ($__auto interpolated in expr before execution) that the production code path intentionally does not perform, giving false confidence and masking regressions in the actual pass-through semantics; a future reader may rely on this assertion as documented behavior.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test asserts an outcome that cannot occur in production, weakening the regression value of the new coverage.
raw_findings.impact: The test certifies behavior ($__auto interpolated in expr before execution) that the production code path intentionally does not perform, giving false confidence and masking regressions in the actual pass-through semantics; a future reader may rely on this assertion as documented behavior.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new test's templateSrv mock bypasses the scopedVars filtering logic of applyTemplateVariables, so the expr assertion validates the mock rather than the datasource behavior.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Assert only the behavior the frontend actually changes (e.g. step: '$step' -> '5m'), or make the mock replace honor the passed variables map so $__auto stays uninterpolated as in production.
raw_findings.title: Test asserts $__auto is interpolated to '5m' although production applyTemplateVariables deliberately excludes __auto from frontend interpolation
raw_findings.trigger: The mock templateSrv.replace unconditionally does input.replace('$__auto', '5m'), ignoring the variables map. The real applyTemplateVariables destructures __auto out of scopedVars ('We want to interpolate these variables on backend'), so in production the expr keeps $__auto and only the backend replaces it.

raw_findings.body: The assertion that the sub-request expr contains '[5m]' passes only because of the over-permissive mock; it does not verify real interpolation behavior for the shard path and can hide a regression where $__auto handling changes.
raw_findings.failure_mode: New test coverage asserts a behavior that diverges from the production code path it claims to verify.
raw_findings.impact: The assertion that the sub-request expr contains '[5m]' passes only because of the over-permissive mock; it does not verify real interpolation behavior for the shard path and can hide a regression where $__auto handling changes.
raw_findings.root_cause: The mock templateSrv.replace short-circuits the scoped-variable exclusion logic inside applyTemplateVariables.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the step assertion but change the expr assertion to expect '[$__auto]' (matching real pass-through behavior), or implement the replace mock to respect the variables map passed by applyTemplateVariables.
raw_findings.title: Shard-split test's $__auto expr assertion relies on a mock that ignores the variables map, misrepresenting production interpolation
raw_findings.trigger: The test's replace mock does input.replace('$__auto', '5m') regardless of the variables argument, but the real applyTemplateVariables removes __auto from scopedVars before calling templateSrv.replace, so production leaves $__auto in the expr for backend interpolation.

finding.title: Queries are interpolated twice: runSplitQuery and DataSourceWithBackend.query both apply applyTemplateVariables, duplicating ad-hoc filters
finding.trigger: A user runs a Loki query with the lokiQuerySplitting feature toggle enabled while ad-hoc filters are active on the dashboard/Explore. runSplitQuery interpolates the targets here, then each sub-request flows through datasource.runQuery -> super.query() (DataSourceWithBackend.query, line 185), which calls applyTemplateVariables again with the same request.filters.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that DataSourceWithBackend.query re-applies applyTemplateVariables is incorrect. Looking at DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185, it only calls applyTemplateVariables when shouldApplyTemplateVariables is true, and line 175 shows shouldApplyTemplateVariables is set to false when the datasource differs. More importantly, runSplitQuery calls datasource.runQuery (line 350), which is LokiDatasource.runQuery (line 350-357), which calls super.query() but the queries passed have already been interpolated and the same targets flow through. The patch does not show evidence of double application - runQuery receives already-interpolated queries.

finding.verifier_reason: The claim of triple application is unsubstantiated. runShardSplitQuery interpolates at line 52, then passes to splitQueriesByStreamShard which calls runSplitQuery at line 163. However, runSplitQuery receives the already-interpolated queries via the subRequest which has targets set from interpolateShardingSelector. The test at line 112 shows applyTemplateVariables is called 5 times total (once per shard group), not three times per target. The claim conflates call count with per-target application count.
